brief.offer: Recruiting and scheduling customer interview participants for product teams

facts.claim: Linear is a product development tool built for modern teams with AI workflows at its core.
facts.excerpt: A new species of product tool. Purpose-built for modern teams with AI workflows at its core, Linear sets a new standard for planning and building products.
facts.source_title: Linear – The system for product development

facts.claim: Linear says it powers more than 40,000 product teams, including startups and enterprises.
facts.excerpt: Linear powers over40,000 product teams. From ambitious startups to major enterprises.
facts.source_title: Linear – The system for product development

facts.claim: Linear includes agent-based workflows and lets teams delegate issues end-to-end to AI agents.
facts.excerpt:
Powered by agents

Designed for workflows shared by humans and agents. From drafting PRDs to pushing PRs. [...] Build and deploy AI agents that work alongside you as teammates. Work on complex tasks together or delegate entire issues end-to-end.
facts.source_title: Linear – The system for product development

facts.claim: Linear is available on web, macOS, Windows, iOS, and Android.
facts.excerpt: Available for web,  macOS, Windows, iOS, and Android.

facts.claim: Linear’s mobile app is a companion to the desktop app and supports on-the-go issue and project updates.
facts.excerpt: Linear Mobile is a companion to the Linear desktop app, designed for on-demand workflows when you are away from your keyboard: • File issues on-the-go • Stay up-to-date on your most important streams of work • Get instant notifications about important updates

research.website_note: Result 1 identifies linear.app as Linear’s official site, so the website belongs to Linear.

strategy.observation: Linear is a product development tool built for product teams, and it says its AI/agent-based workflows are now core to the product.
strategy.offer_link: If Linear is evolving its own AI and agent workflows, your product team may need a steady flow of customer interviews to validate how product teams actually use those experiences, and we can handle recruiting and scheduling those participants.
hypotheses: I’m assuming your team runs customer interviews as part of product discovery and roadmap validation.
I’m assuming you’d want to hear from current Linear users or similar product teams, not generic consumers.
I’m assuming coordinating interviewees is still a meaningful time sink for the product team.
strategy.angle: With Linear pushing agent-based workflows, I thought it could be useful to make customer interview recruiting and scheduling easier for your product team.
strategy.fit_reason: Linear is a product tool for product teams, so recruiting interview participants is plausibly useful to the Head of Product for research and validation, especially as the company leans further into AI and agent-based workflows.

draft.subject: Customer interviews at Linear
draft.body:
Hi,

Linear’s AI and agent workflows seem central now. If your team is validating how product teams use them, my guess is interview recruiting and scheduling still takes real time.

We handle recruiting and scheduling customer interview participants for product teams, so the team can spend more time on the actual conversations.

Who owns that recruiting work on your side today?
